experiments.label: Caffeine in coffee
experiments.requirements: Check the installed column and UV detector. Distinguish extract concentration from caffeine per mass of coffee.

experiments.label: Sweeteners in diet drinks
experiments.requirements: Choose the target sweeteners before comparing separations. Confirm the detector can measure each compound and check recovery in the beverage.

experiments.label: Identify microplastic polymers
experiments.q: Identify a polymer using infrared spectra
experiments.requirements: The drinking-water procedure needs microscopy and optics appropriate to particle size. Bench ATR can support bulk reference spectra; confirm the installed accessory before planning particle imaging.

experiments.label: Screen flour identity by infrared spectra
experiments.q: Screen wheat flour identity by infrared spectra
experiments.requirements: Requires diamond ATR for the cited Cary workflow. Use representative flours and independent test mixtures to check the spectral classification.

experiments.label: Cyanocobalamin identity
experiments.requirements: Use a suitable quartz cell and reference standard. Identity, calibration of pure standards and analysis of a food extract answer different questions.

experiments.label: Orthophosphate colorimetry
experiments.requirements: Match the calibration range and optical path to the method. Confirm a suitable cuvette and check for matrix effects before measuring unknowns.

experiments.label: Water pH
experiments.requirements: Select an appropriate pH electrode, buffers and temperature measurement. Low-ionic-strength water needs particular attention to electrode response.

experiments.label: Soil pH by water extraction
experiments.q: Measure soil pH in a water extract
experiments.requirements: Record the soil-to-water ratio, electrode, calibration and temperature. Soil pH values depend on the extraction method.

experiments.label: Water conductivity
experiments.q: Check water conductivity against a standard
experiments.requirements: Use the correct conductivity cell, calibration standard and temperature basis. Predicting conductance independently also requires the dissolved-ion composition.

experiments.label: Soil salinity by conductivity
experiments.requirements: Use the specified extract ratio and report the temperature basis. Comparing this with a saturated-paste value requires evidence for the soils being tested.

experiments.label: Suspended solids by mass
experiments.q: Determine suspended solids in water by gravimetry
experiments.requirements: Requires suitable filter media and drying equipment as well as a balance. Select a representative subsample and check the expected mass gain against the balance resolution.

experiments.label: Mineral soil moisture by mass
experiments.requirements: Requires both an oven and a balance sized for the container. For the UF55, confirm the mineral load is noncombustible and within its intended use. Report the dry-mass basis.

experiments.label: Flour moisture by loss on drying
experiments.requirements: Use a balance that can take the loaded dish and a separate oven suitable for flour. The UF55 is restricted to noncombustible loads.

experiments.label: Coarse aggregate water absorption
experiments.requirements: Use noncombustible coarse mineral aggregate within the oven load limit. You also need a balance sized for the bulk specimen, a basket and an immersion tank.

experiments.label: Honey moisture by refractive index
experiments.requirements: Use the refractive index and honey-specific conversion at the appropriate temperature. A sucrose Brix reading alone is insufficient.

experiments.label: Cactus pear juice soluble solids
experiments.requirements: Use representative clarified juice, verify the zero and record the Brix scale. Other dissolved substances contribute to the reading.

experiments.label: Grape juice ripeness by Brix
experiments.requirements: Document berry sampling, juice extraction, scale and temperature. Within-bunch variation can exceed instrument repeatability.

experiments.label: Honey pollen microscopy
experiments.requirements: Check transmitted-light optics, slide preparation and the pollen reference collection. Automated classifications also require a suitable imaging system.

experiments.label: Leaf stomatal density
experiments.requirements: Calibrate the viewed field area and record the leaf side, preparation and sampling scheme. Comparing counts requires a common area basis.

experiments.label: Jar-test coagulation by turbidity
experiments.requirements: Requires a jar-test setup and consistent settling and sampling. Record the meter’s light source and reporting unit when comparing studies.

experiments.label: Suspended sediment from turbidity
experiments.requirements: Collect paired local turbidity and reference sediment measurements across the range. A published slope or a continuous-sensor calibration requires local verification on a portable meter.

experiments.label: Kombucha ethanol by headspace GC
experiments.requirements: Check headspace sampling and the selected detector, column and alcohol standards. This experiment measures a beverage sample.

experiments.label: Fatty acid profiles of vegetable oils
experiments.q: Compare fatty acids in vegetable oils
experiments.requirements: Requires suitable FAME preparation, a capillary column, a flame ionization detector and reference standards. Confirm resolution of the target isomers.

experiments.label: Aroma volatiles in olive oil
experiments.q: Measure aroma volatiles in virgin olive oil
experiments.requirements: Confirm headspace SPME equipment, fiber, column and detector. Analyte identification and detector response depend on the chosen configuration.

experiments.label: Pipette delivery by weighing water
experiments.requirements: Use a calibrated balance with sufficient resolution at the chosen volume and control evaporation. Compare like volumes, compatible tips and the limits for the exact pipette.

experiments.label: Pipetting precision with dye dilutions
experiments.requirements: For the quantitative plate exercise, provide a compatible reader and both pipette ranges when specified. The tube exercise provides a visual dilution check. Check every transfer against the pipette range.
